text:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME-ops reported invalid JSON when using json_mode=strict. They see a parse error 'unexpected token ',' in number' from our parser. Customer pasted a failing response sample.

jason_acme: 'We call /v1/generate with our schema expecting integer price. Sometimes the model emits locale-formatted numbers with commas like 1,234 which breaks parsing. It's intermittent (~8-12% of calls).

maria_support: Sample failed response they sent (note the unquoted comma in numeric literal):
```json
{
  "id": 12345,
  "items": [
    {"name":"widget","price": 1,234, "status":"active"}
  ]
}
```

kevin_eng: Thanks — this looks like locale-formatted numbers slipping into model outputs. Our JSON parser treats commas inside number tokens as invalid JSON. Can you confirm model + params (temp, stream) and whether you ever see trailing percent signs or currency symbols? Streaming chops can also create partial numbers (e.g. '1,23') that break the parser.

jason_acme: We're on `gpt-neox-3.7` (redwood-curated), temp=0.2, stream=false. It spikes when the item list is long or prompts include example outputs with commas. We also occasionally see values like "12.3%" or currency prefixes.

kevin_eng: Short-term client-side mitigations: 1) accept numbers as strings in your schema ("price": "1234"); 2) sanitize the raw model text before JSON.parse: strip thousands separators and percent signs, then parse. Example (JS):
```js
const cleaned = rawText.replace(/(\d),(?=\d{3})/g, '$1').replace(/%/g, '');
const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);
```
This handles common comma-grouped thousands (1,234 -> 1234) and removes % for numeric fields.

kevin_eng: I've opened an eng-runtime ticket to add optional pre-parse normalization when json_mode=strict is enabled: - strip localized grouping separators inside numeric tokens - remove common unit suffixes (%,$) if schema expects numbers - try coercing numeric strings to numbers when the schema allows it. Will include tests for stream vs non-stream.

ops_bot: created INC-2026-234: "json_mode.strict - locale-formatted numbers causing parse errors" (priority: P2)

maria_support: @kevin_eng can you add a quick repro harness (prompt + call) and test across model variants + temp ranges? @jason_acme we'll try the client-side sanitizer as a stopgap and follow up once eng posts a patch. Thanks :thumbsup:

kevin_eng: Will do — I'll attach a minimal repro curl in the ticket and run it across gpt-neox-3.7 and gpt-j-2.0 to see if this is model-specific or prompt-triggered.

jason_acme: Appreciate it, thanks for the quick response. We'll implement the sanitizer for now and let you know if we see other localized formats (dots as thousands separators, non-breaking spaces, etc.).
